label: Early original-phase step (t=2-3) after a leading digit 0
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase at fixed early positions: t=3 (75% of mass), t=2 (20%), t=4 (5%); never at t<2, t>=5, at <DEL>, or during copy. It is gated by a digit 0 at the very start of the sequence: first_tok=0 has 15.5x lift (67% of mass) and prev2_tok=0 has 17.5x lift. The predicate (t=3 with 0 at position 0 or 1, or t=2 with 0 at position 0) gets dev precision 0.93, recall 0.66, mass recall 0.88. The strongest activations (~2.7) are sequences starting 0 0 e, at t=3, with a weaker echo at t=4. Which token is input at the firing step barely matters. Remaining misses are weak t=3 activations with no leading 0 (rate about 1-2%, usually <0.1 of max) and t=4 activations in 0-initial sequences. A 0 at position 2 or later does not reliably trigger it.

issues: The main claims hold up. Firing is almost entirely in the original phase: share of activation mass is 0.196 at t=2, 0.749 at t=3 and 0.055 at t=4. It never fires in the copy phase (0 of 2.7M steps), and fires only 14 times at <DEL> and 12 times at t=5. first_tok=0 has 15.5x lift and prev2_tok=0 has 17.5x lift. On the test split the original predicate scores P=0.933, R=0.659, F1=0.772, mass recall 0.878.

There is a systematic miss class, and the explanation understates it. At t=3 in sequences with no 0 at position 0 or 1, the feature fires at a rate of 3.7%, not the claimed 1-2%. That class is 24% of all active steps (6.5% of mass). It depends on the first token in a graded way: orig(0)=d fires 22.6% of the time, i 21.6%, f 10.8%, m/a/b about 8%, h/w/y about 5%. Several first tokens (j,k,n,p,r,s,t,v and the digits 3/2/1) are near 0%. So the weak firings are a first-token-identity effect, not scattered noise. Adding it to the predicate (t==3 & orig(0) in {d,i}) lowers precision to 0.66 (test F1 0.703), so it stays a low-magnitude side effect that is best mentioned rather than encoded.

The t=4 misses are partly systematic. t=4 with orig(0)==0 and orig(1)==0 has P=0.994, and with orig(0)==0 and orig(2)==0 has P=0.980. t=4 with any leading 0 has only P=0.276. Adding the two-zero t=4 clause raises test F1 from 0.772 to 0.782 and mass recall to 0.901.

The label overclaims a little: 'after a leading digit 0' leaves out the predicate's t=3 case where position 1 is 0 and position 0 is not. That case is 25% of mass but less precise (P=0.866). The FPs are of the form 't 0 w *0*' and 'k 0 a *e*'. There is also an asymmetry: at t=2, orig(1)==0 without orig(0)==0 never fires (P=0.000). The label should say that only position 0 counts at t=2.

Smaller points: 'never fires at <DEL>' is effectively true (14 steps). 'A 0 at position 2 does not reliably trigger it' is confirmed (t=3 & orig(2)==0: P=0.23). In the test misses, a 0 at position 2 does add a t=4 echo, e.g. '0 c 0 d d' gives 0.56 at t=3 and 0.31 at t=4.
